sentences.zh: 食貨三 ○歲賜

translations.literal: Food and Goods 3 ○ Annual Stipends
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics 3 ○ Annual Stipends

sentences.zh: 自昔帝王於其宗族姻戚必致其厚者，所以明親親之義也。

translations.literal: From antiquity emperors toward their clansmen and affinal kin necessarily extended the utmost generosity—this was to make clear the meaning of cherishing one's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, emperors have lavished generosity on their clansmen and affinal kin in order to embody the principle of cherishing one's own kin.

sentences.zh: 元之為制，其又厚之至者歟！

translations.literal: As for the Yuan institution, was it not generosity carried to the utmost!
translations.idiomatic: Among all such institutions, was any ever more lavish than that of the Yuan!

sentences.zh: 凡諸王及后妃公主，皆有食采分地。

translations.literal: All princes, as well as empresses, consorts, and princesses, all had fiefs for sustenance and allotted lands.
translations.idiomatic: Every prince, empress, consort, and princess received a sustenance fief and allotted lands.

sentences.zh: 其路府州縣得薦其私人以為監，秩祿受命如王官，而不得以歲月通選調。

translations.literal: Their circuits, prefectures, districts, and counties could recommend their private retainers to serve as supervisors; rank and salary were received on appointment like princely officials, yet they could not advance through the regular selection and transfer system by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Their circuits, prefectures, districts, and counties might recommend private retainers as supervisors, who received rank and salary like princely officials but could not advance through the regular civil-service rotation.

sentences.zh: 其賦則五戶出絲一斤，不得私征之，皆輸諸有司之府，視所當得之數而給與之。

translations.literal: Their levy was one jin of silk from every five households; private collection was not permitted—all was delivered to the appropriate government treasury, and disbursement was made according to the amount due.
translations.idiomatic: Their levy was one jin of silk per five households. Private collection was forbidden; all revenue went to the appropriate government treasury, which disbursed what each recipient was due.

sentences.zh: 其歲賜則銀幣各有差，始定於太宗之時，而增於憲宗之日。

translations.literal: Their annual stipends in silver and currency each had graded amounts, first fixed in the time of Taizong and increased in the days of Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Annual stipends in silver and currency varied by rank, first fixed under Emperor Taizong (Ögedei) and later increased under Emperor Xianzong (Möngke).

sentences.zh: 及世祖平江南，又各益以民戶。

translations.literal: When Shizu pacified the Jiangnan, each was further augmented with civilian households.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shizu (Kublai) pacified the Jiangnan, each recipient was further granted civilian households.

sentences.zh: 時科差未定，每戶折支中統鈔五錢，至成宗復加至二貫。

translations.literal: At the time corvée levies were not yet fixed; each household was paid out in Zhongtong notes at five qian, and under Chengzong this was again raised to two guan.
translations.idiomatic: While corvée quotas were still unsettled, each household was assessed at five qian in Zhongtong paper notes; under Emperor Chengzong this was raised to two guan.

sentences.zh: 其親親之義若此，誠可謂厚之至矣。

translations.literal: Their meaning of cherishing kin was like this—truly it may be called generosity to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: In cherishing kin they went this far—truly generosity carried to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 至於勛臣亦然，又所以大報功也。

translations.literal: As for meritorious ministers it was likewise—this was again how great service was greatly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ministers were treated likewise, for this was how great deeds received great reward.

sentences.zh: 故詳著其所賜之人，及其數之多寡於後。

translations.literal: Therefore the persons granted and the greater or lesser amounts are set forth in detail below.
translations.idiomatic: The recipients and the amounts granted to each are therefore recorded in detail below.
